titleText.es: Además, ¿soy sólo yo, o Japón y Nueva Zelanda son sospechosamente parecidas? ¿Alguien las ha visto juntas en una fiesta alguna vez?
titleText.en: Also, is it just me, or do Japan and New Zealand look suspiciously similar?  Has anyone seen them at a party together?
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive supplies a faithful translated title text. The official English JSON contains two spaces between its questions; they are preserved here.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Oeste names the direction where the sun sets. This literal direction is distinct from el Oeste used as a broad cultural or geopolitical label.

example.es: El barco navega hacia el oeste.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: the East; a broad eastern geographic or cultural region
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Este can name the compass direction or, by convention, a broad geographic or cultural region. The article el is used because the word is acting as a noun; context, not the article alone, selects the regional sense.

example.es: El libro compara el este con el oeste.
example.en: The book compares the East with the West.

cardDefinitions.answerEn: the West; a broad western geographic or cultural region
cardDefinitions.noteEn: Oeste can name the compass direction or, by convention, a broad geographic or cultural region. The article el is used because the word is acting as a noun; context, not the article alone, selects the regional sense.

example.es: El texto habla de relaciones entre el este y el oeste.
example.en: The text discusses relations between the East and the West.

cardDefinitions.noteEn: Fastidiado is the completed-action form of fastidiar, ‘to annoy’ or ‘to bother.’ After a form of haber such as ha, it stays unchanged.

example.es: Ese ruido me ha fastidiado todo el día.
example.en: That noise has bothered me all day.

cardDefinitions.promptEs: el este y el oeste como regiones culturales
cardDefinitions.questionEn: Why can “the East” lie west of someone while “the West” lies east of them?
cardDefinitions.answerEn: These are conventional cultural and geographic labels, not directions measured from the current observer.
cardDefinitions.noteEn: The labels grew from a Europe-centered view: East Asia became ‘the East,’ while Europe and societies historically grouped with it became ‘the West.’ From North America, traveling toward East Asia can mean going west across the Pacific, while traveling toward Europe can mean going east across the Atlantic. That mismatch creates the joke.

example.es: Desde California, Japón queda al oeste.
example.en: From California, Japan lies to the west.
